# Skinpal

> Skinpal is a mobile app and community for people living with topical steroid withdrawal (TSW) and eczema. Users log their day in one tap or by talking (voice logging; audio is never stored), mark symptoms on a body map, and see good and bad periods in a calendar coloured by itch. AI insights: Skinpal's AI writes daily and weekly insights in plain words, based only on the user's own logs, and a 90-day report can be shared with a doctor. A community inside the app connects people going through the same thing. Skinpal does not give medical advice, diagnose or recommend treatment.

## Key facts

- Made by TSW Nordic AB, Gothenburg, Sweden.
- Founded by Lukas Löfgren, who has lived with TSW since January 2022 and shares his story on Instagram as @tswlukas (40,000+ followers across platforms).
- Platforms: iPhone (App Store) and Android (Google Play).
- Languages: English and Spanish.
- Price: 14-day free trial, then $3.99 per month or $39.99 per year (USD).
- Data: encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS. Never sold. Users can delete their account and health data at any time.
- Who it is for: adults with topical steroid withdrawal, eczema (atopic dermatitis) or similar long-running skin conditions who want a simple daily record to look back on and share with their doctor.

## Main features

- One-tap logging ("same as yesterday") and voice logging: say how the day was and Skinpal fills in the log. The mic only listens when tapped and audio is never stored.
- Body map: mark several areas at once; itch on a 0 to 10 scale, sleep, mood, stress, food, notes and photos.
- Calendar coloured by itch, showing good and bad periods at a glance.
- AI insights: daily and weekly insights written by AI from the user's own logs only, to answer "is it better than last month?" The AI does not diagnose or give medical advice.
- 90-day report to bring to a doctor, with notes and photos only if the user chooses.
- Community inside the app, with spaces for TSW, for parents and for the emotional side of living with a skin condition.
- Current version: 2.3 (November 2026), with a redesigned, calmer interface.
